rules: The server resolves source scope and import authority before adopting the object.
The original bytes and sha256 are retained; client MIME and filename are not format proof.
A committed upload returns objectId; a commit-unknown result is retried by the same operationId only.
The object must belong to sourceId and must be parsed with sop-xlsx-v1.
The parser returns all six worksheet categories, row text and same-row media references.
A blocking issue returns no usable rows or attachments and creates no publishable candidate.
sourceId plus explicit version or raw file sha256 is the idempotency key.
A replay returns the existing candidate or the existing operation result without duplicate media links.
Media references are immutable after the candidate digest is fixed.
The response does not expose object-store keys or permanent URLs.
Rows and attachments are returned only when the caller has the candidate source scope.
The server rechecks source mode, import/publish authority, quality state, candidate digest and base release.
Every SopMediaRef must be adopted and bound to the same source before the release transaction starts.
Release rows and release-media links are committed atomically; no partial text-only or media-only release is valid.
The confirmation dialog expresses user intent only; it is not approval evidence.
COMMIT_UNKNOWN is returned as 503 and keeps the operationId for recovery.
The server checks current product session, entitlement, release scope, release-media link and media state on every request.
An absent or inaccessible concrete release/media pair returns the same 404 NOT_FOUND result.
The response never redirects to an external URL and never grants a reusable object-store URL.
Copy actions operate on the row text; media preview is a separate read and is never copied as answer text.
The rollback plan includes every source and media link in the target release.
Partial source loss is an all-release refusal and maps to 403 SCOPE_DENIED; complete loss maps to 404 NOT_FOUND.
Rollback creates a new release lineage and does not mutate the historical release or attachment rows.
A media link cannot be removed while a protected release or active entitlement references it.
The lookup is bound to the current session, action and operation namespace.
Unknown commit is recovered with the original operationId; a new key does not create a second publish.
Permission loss after a confirmed commit cannot erase the committed object or release; it only blocks later replay/read.

fields.sheet: one of the six exact worksheet names
